paper.abstract: Visual grounding models can enhance radiology workflows by linking report findings to image regions. This is particularly valuable for 3D CT, where findings often occupy a tiny fraction of the volume. Training 3D grounding models requires large sets of paired phrases and regions, and building such datasets is expensive, requiring radiologists to annotate images by hand. We posit that this supervision is already created implicitly during routine reporting, as radiologists frequently place 2D annotations (e.g., distance measurement, arrows) on key images to make measurements and to support report interpretation. We introduce an automated pipeline that converts these routine clinical annotations into large-scale phrase-region supervision for 3D visual grounding. The pipeline links each annotation to the corresponding finding in the report through metadata matching, then uses a promptable 3D segmentation model to convert the 2D annotation into a volumetric mask. This produces phrase-mask-volume datasets without requiring additional radiologist annotation. Applied to a single institution's clinical picture archiving and communication system (PACS), our approach generated 105K phrase-mask-volume triplets from 59K abdominal CT exams. We also introduce two abdominal CT grounding benchmarks, LocusBench-Onc and LocusBench-ED, which comprise 240 oncology and 260 emergency-department radiologist-reviewed phrase-mask-volume triplets, respectively, with the latter spanning 13 distinct categories such as appendicitis, hematoma, and hernia. We further introduce LocusCT, a 3D visual grounding model trained on this dataset, which achieves hit rates of 0.725 on LocusBench-Onc and 0.773 on LocusBench-ED, substantially outperforming comparator models. These results show that routine PACS annotations are a scalable, previously unused source of supervision for 3D visual grounding.
paper.title: Scaling 3D Visual Grounding in Abdominal CT

translation.abstract_zh: 视觉定位模型可以通过将报告中的发现与图像区域关联来增强放射学工作流程。这对于3D CT尤其有价值，因为病灶通常只占据体积的一小部分。训练3D定位模型需要大量成对的短语和区域，而构建此类数据集成本高昂，需要放射科医生手动标注图像。我们认为，这种监督信号在常规报告过程中已经被隐式创建，因为放射科医生经常在关键图像上放置2D标注（例如距离测量、箭头）以进行测量并支持报告解读。我们引入了一个自动化流程，将这些常规临床标注转换为用于3D视觉定位的大规模短语-区域监督。该流程通过元数据匹配将每个标注与报告中相应的发现关联起来，然后使用可提示的3D分割模型将2D标注转换为体积掩膜。这生成了短语-掩膜-体积数据集，而无需额外的放射科医生标注。应用于单一机构的临床图像归档和通信系统（PACS），我们的方法从59K次腹部CT检查中生成了105K个短语-掩膜-体积三元组。我们还引入了两个腹部CT定位基准，LocusBench-Onc和LocusBench-ED，分别包含240个肿瘤学和260个急诊科放射科医生审核的短语-掩膜-体积三元组，后者涵盖13个不同类别，如阑尾炎、血肿和疝气。我们进一步引入了LocusCT，一个在该数据集上训练的3D视觉定位模型，在LocusBench-Onc上达到0.725的命中率，在LocusBench-ED上达到0.773，大幅优于对比模型。这些结果表明，常规PACS标注是一种可扩展的、此前未被使用的3D视觉定位监督来源。
translation.title_zh: 在腹部CT中扩展3D视觉定位

paper.abstract: Accurate three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction of individual dendrites in serial block-face scanning electron microscopy (SBF-SEM) is essential for quantifying structural plasticity in the brain, yet manual annotation at scale is infeasible. We present a fully automatic pipeline for 3D dendrite instance segmentation that unifies YOLOv6-guided Segment Anything Model (SAM) prompting on downsampled slices, iterative two-dimensional mask refinement, random forest 3D instance linking, and instance-aware high-resolution refinement using nnU-Net at native resolution into a single system requiring no manual prompting at inference. Applied to hippocampal CA1 SBF-SEM datasets from a control rat and a pilocarpine- induced epileptic rat, our pipeline reconstructs coherent, well- separated dendrites with high semantic accuracy (Dice 0.93 and 0.91) and strong instance-level performance on control tissue, while analysis of the more challenging epileptic tissue identifies instance recognition in dense regions as the principal remaining limitation. The high-resolution refinement stage recovers thin dendritic protrusions, providing a basis for downstream spine- level analysis. Code is available at https://github.com/ ZE-WEN/dendrite-3d-instance-seg.
paper.title: A Fully Automatic Pipeline for 3D Dendrite Instance Segmentation in SBF-SEM

translation.abstract_zh: 在连续块面扫描电子显微镜（SBF-SEM）中，对单个树突进行精确的三维（3D）重建对于量化大脑中的结构可塑性至关重要，但大规模人工标注不可行。我们提出了一条用于3D树突实例分割的全自动管线，将降采样切片上的YOLOv6引导的Segment Anything Model（SAM）提示、迭代二维掩膜细化、随机森林3D实例连接，以及在原生分辨率下使用nnU-Net进行的实例感知高分辨率细化统一为一个系统，推理时无需人工提示。将该管线应用于来自对照大鼠和匹罗卡品诱导癫痫大鼠的海马CA1 SBF-SEM数据集，我们的管线重建出连贯且分离良好的树突，具有较高的语义准确性（Dice 0.93和0.91），并在对照组织上展现出强大的实例级性能，而对更具挑战性的癫痫组织的分析则表明，密集区域中的实例识别是主要的剩余局限。高分辨率细化阶段恢复了纤细的树突突起，为下游的树突棘水平分析提供了基础。代码可在https://github.com/ZE-WEN/dendrite-3d-instance-seg获取。
translation.title_zh: SBF-SEM中三维树突实例分割的全自动管线

paper.abstract: Automatic horizon tracking is a foundational task in 3D seismic interpretation. Most existing deep learning approaches formulate it as dense semantic segmentation, typically using U-Net-based architectures. The model produces a probability map over all pixels that must be post-processed to extract precise horizon coordinates, while horizon picks in time/depth must be converted into dense masks for training. Unpicked seismic traces are consequently treated as background, which can hinder convergence, and both pre- and post-processing can introduce errors into the final interpretation. Moreover, 2D segmentation models do not inherently capture inter-slice context, while 3D models are often computationally prohibitive. We instead formulate horizon tracking as a bounded coordinate regression problem, where the model directly predicts the time/depth coordinate of the target horizon at each lateral position. We propose a lightweight regression head compatible with any pretrained vision backbone, coupled with an LSTM module to model inter-slice context and produce a continuous horizon surface across the volume. A combination of L1 and L2 losses supervises predictions at valid horizon picks, while a geology-informed regularization enforces lateral continuity between successive traces. Under controlled experimental conditions, we evaluate four pretrained vision backbones under both segmentation and regression configurations on a seismic volume from New Zealand. The proposed approach consistently outperforms its segmentation counterparts quantitatively, using metrics including RMSE and PCC, and qualitatively, while also demonstrating greater robustness to increasing sparsity of training picks. Finally, we show that prediction variation across successive traces captures local variations in geological complexity, providing an automated quality control measure for downstream seismic interpretation.
paper.title: DeepStratNet: A Context-Aware Coordinate Regression Framework for Seismic Horizon Tracking under Sparse Labels

translation.abstract_zh: 自动层位追踪是三维地震解释中的一项基础任务。大多数现有深度学习方法将其表述为密集语义分割，通常使用基于U-Net的架构。该模型在所有像素上产生概率图，必须经过后处理才能提取精确的层位坐标，而时间/深度上的层位拾取必须转换为密集掩码以进行训练。因此，未拾取的地震道被视为背景，这可能阻碍收敛，并且预处理和后处理都可能给最终解释引入误差。此外，二维分割模型本质上无法捕捉切片间上下文，而三维模型通常在计算上难以承受。我们转而将层位追踪表述为有界坐标回归问题，其中模型直接预测每个横向位置上目标层位的时间/深度坐标。我们提出了一种轻量级回归头，可与任何预训练视觉骨干网络兼容，并结合LSTM模块来建模切片间上下文，从而在整个数据体上生成连续的层位表面。L1和L2损失的组合在有效层位拾取处监督预测，而地质信息正则化则强制连续道之间的横向连续性。在受控实验条件下，我们在来自新西兰的一个地震数据体上，评估了四种预训练视觉骨干网络在分割和回归配置下的表现。所提出的方法在定量指标（包括RMSE和PCC）和定性方面均持续优于其分割对应方法，同时还表现出对训练拾取稀疏性增加的更强鲁棒性。最后，我们表明连续道之间的预测变化捕捉了地质复杂性的局部变化，为下游地震解释提供了一种自动质量控制措施。
translation.title_zh: DeepStratNet：一种用于稀疏标签下地震层位追踪的上下文感知坐标回归框架

paper.abstract: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR), including cine imaging, is a reference standard for the noninvasive assessment of cardiac morphology and ventricular function. Cine CMR interpretation integrates qualitative visual assessment with quantitative measurements of ventricular volumes, ejection fraction, myocardial mass, wall thickness, and regional wall motion. Current medical vision-language models (VLMs) cannot reliably derive quantitative measurements from multidimensional cine images without analysis tools. We present CineMR, a tool-augmented VLM that invokes cardiac image-analysis tools and integrates their outputs into interleaved reasoning for quantitative CMR assessment. We also construct a multi-cohort visual question answering benchmark covering quantitative metric extraction, multiclass diagnosis, and differential diagnosis, together with tools for segmentation, phase selection, volumetry, morphometry, and regional wall motion analysis. CineMR is trained with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on tool-interaction traces followed by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with conditional tool-use rewards. On the multi-cohort cine CMR benchmark, CineMR achieves 35.9% pass@1 and 58.9% pass@4, compared with 1.5% pass@1 for the Qwen3-VL-8B backbone and 0.0% and 7.0% pass@1 for LLaVA-Med v1.5 and MedGemma-4B, respectively. Correct tool invocation reaches 99.8% after GRPO, up from 78.9% after SFT. Live tool outputs improve ventricular measurement accuracy by 20.4--23.7% over direct model predictions, and removing all tools reduces pass@1 from 35.9% to 27.9%. These results highlight the importance of reliable tool use for quantitative cine CMR reasoning and support CineMR as a promising approach for assistive cardiac image assessment. Code, benchmark resources, and model weights are available at https://github.com/AI-MIND-Lab/CineMR.
paper.title: CineMR: Tool-Integrated Vision-Language Reasoning for Quantitative Cardiac MRI Assessment

translation.abstract_zh: 心血管磁共振（CMR），包括电影成像，是无创评估心脏形态和心室功能的参考标准。电影CMR解读将定性视觉评估与心室容积、射血分数、心肌质量、室壁厚度和局部室壁运动的定量测量相结合。当前的医学视觉-语言模型（VLM）无法在没有分析工具的情况下从多维电影图像中可靠地得出定量测量。我们提出CineMR，一种工具增强的VLM，它调用心脏图像分析工具并将其输出整合到交错推理中，以进行定量CMR评估。我们还构建了一个多队列视觉问答基准，涵盖定量指标提取、多分类诊断和鉴别诊断，以及用于分割、时相选择、容量测定、形态测量和局部室壁运动分析的工具。CineMR首先在工具交互轨迹上进行监督微调（SFT），然后使用带有条件工具使用奖励的组相对策略优化（GRPO）进行训练。在多队列电影CMR基准上，CineMR达到35.9%的pass@1和58.9%的pass@4，而Qwen3-VL-8B主干为1.5%的pass@1，LLaVA-Med v1.5和MedGemma-4B分别为0.0%和7.0%的pass@1。经过GRPO后，正确的工具调用率达到99.8%，高于SFT后的78.9%。实时工具输出将心室测量准确率比直接模型预测提高了20.4–23.7%，而移除所有工具会将pass@1从35.9%降至27.9%。这些结果凸显了可靠工具使用对定量电影CMR推理的重要性，并支持CineMR作为辅助心脏图像评估的一种有前景的方法。代码、基准资源和模型权重可在https://github.com/AI-MIND-Lab/CineMR获取。
translation.title_zh: CineMR：面向定量心脏MRI评估的工具集成视觉-语言推理

paper.abstract: Scientific image segmentation methods rely on extensive annotation and task-specific training, limiting adaptation across imaging modalities and experimental conditions. We present a training-free, one-shot framework that specializes vision foundation models using a single annotated reference image. The framework combines DINOv3 representations with background-adaptive feature orthogonalization to suppress artifact-related feature directions, after which cosine similarity localizes candidate regions for SAM segmentation. We evaluate the framework on red-blood-cell microscopy, structured-illumination pool boiling, and chest radiography. Relative to the strongest baseline, the proposed method improves mean IoU by 5.91% and 78.62% on the microscopy and pool-boiling datasets, respectively, while achieving comparable performance on chest radiographs. These results demonstrate that one-shot reference conditioning can adapt general-purpose vision models to specialized scientific segmentation tasks.
paper.title: One-Shot Adaptive Segmentation For Scientific Images

translation.abstract_zh: 科学图像分割方法依赖大量标注和针对特定任务的训练，限制了其在不同成像模态和实验条件下的适应性。我们提出了一种免训练的一次性框架，利用单张带标注的参考图像使视觉基础模型专门化。该框架将DINOv3表示与背景自适应特征正交化相结合，以抑制与伪影相关的特征方向，随后通过余弦相似度定位候选区域，用于SAM分割。我们在红细胞显微镜、结构光照池沸腾和胸部X射线摄影上评估了该框架。相对于最强的基线，所提方法在显微镜和池沸腾数据集上分别将平均IoU提高了5.91%和78.62%，同时在胸部X射线摄影上取得了相当的性能。这些结果表明，一次性参考条件化能够使通用视觉模型适应专门化的科学分割任务。
translation.title_zh: 面向科学图像的一次性自适应分割

paper.abstract: Referring Expression Segmentation (RES) links natural-language descriptions to pixel-level object masks. Yet standard evaluation provides limited insight into instance-level referential reasoning: it does not systematically distinguish referential logics, test target preservation across valid grounding paths, or separate target-selection from mask-generation errors. We introduce InstanceBench, an instance-centered diagnostic benchmark comprising 6,194 images, 9,264 target instances, and 25,077 human-verified expressions. Each target-centric expression set (TCES) fixes the image and target mask while pairing a minimal expression with a same-target variant that uses another valid cue or grounding path. A compact referential-logic taxonomy spans direct target evidence, same-class selection, relational and compositional grounding, and exclusion, while logic-critical construction suppresses simpler shortcuts. Identity-aware metrics measure target retention and set-level success while separating selection from mask-generation errors. Across 22 native-mask RES checkpoints from 18 model families, the strongest checkpoint reaches 67.1% mIoU but only 59.6% All@0.7. Controlled interventions confirm language sensitivity, while failure decomposition identifies target selection rather than mask decoding as the main bottleneck. On a controlled training subset, matched supervision improves identity-aware performance, showing that the diagnosed capability responds to targeted supervision. Collectively, InstanceBench supports a measure-diagnose-improve cycle: measuring target consistency across grounding paths, localizing failure sources, and evaluating targeted interventions.
paper.title: InstanceBench: Diagnosing Referential Reasoning and Target Identity in Referring Expression Segmentation

translation.abstract_zh: 指称表达分割（RES）将自然语言描述与像素级物体掩码关联起来。然而，标准评估对实例级指称推理的洞察有限：它没有系统地区分指称逻辑、测试目标在有效定位路径间的保持性，也没有将目标选择错误与掩码生成错误分离。我们提出了 InstanceBench，一个以实例为中心的诊断基准，包含 6,194 张图像、9,264 个目标实例和 25,077 条经人工验证的表达。每个以目标为中心的表达集（TCES）固定图像和目标掩码，同时将一个最小表达与一个使用另一有效线索或定位路径的同目标变体配对。一个紧凑的指称逻辑分类体系涵盖直接目标证据、同类选择、关系与组合定位以及排除，而逻辑关键的构造抑制了更简单的捷径。身份感知指标衡量目标保持率和集合级成功率，同时将选择错误与掩码生成错误分离。在来自 18 个模型家族的 22 个原生掩码 RES 检查点上，最强的检查点达到 67.1% mIoU，但 All@0.7 仅为 59.6%。受控干预确认了语言敏感性，而失败分解将目标选择而非掩码解码确定为主要瓶颈。在受控训练子集上，匹配的监督提升了身份感知性能，表明所诊断的能力对有针对性的监督有响应。总体而言，InstanceBench 支持一个测量-诊断-改进的循环：测量跨定位路径的目标一致性、定位失败来源并评估有针对性的干预。
translation.title_zh: InstanceBench：诊断指称表达分割中的指称推理与目标身份

paper.abstract: Reliable volumetric segmentation is critical for clinical diagnostics, yet foundation models such as MedSAM remain deterministic and lack calibrated uncertainty under distribution shift. Existing conformal prediction methods offer statistical guarantees but are frequently applied in 2D and assume symmetric error distributions, so they do not capture the class-specific biases that arise in 3D multi-class segmentation. We propose Class-Aware Asymmetric Weighted Conformal Prediction (CA-WCP), which combines latent-space density-ratio weighting for covariate shift with directional quantiles for the lower and upper volume bounds, and scales each bound by a class-specific asymmetry factor derived from validation-set false-positive and false-negative rates. We prove that CA-WCP retains the weighted-exchangeability marginal coverage guarantee for every class, and we evaluate it on 3D brain tumor segmentation (BraTS 2020) and on a synthetic multi-organ CT benchmark constructed under covariate shift. On both benchmarks the 95\% Clopper--Pearson interval for the observed coverage of CA-WCP contains the nominal 90\% level for every semantic class, while interval width is reduced by 8--14\% relative to symmetric weighted conformal prediction. We further encode the calibrated intervals into structured prompts for a multimodal large language model to produce uncertainty-conditioned radiology reports, linking distribution-shift-aware uncertainty quantification to interpretable clinical communication.
paper.title: Quantifying Volumetric Risk: Class-Aware Asymmetric Weighted Conformal Prediction for 3D Medical Image Segmentation

translation.abstract_zh: 可靠的体积分割对于临床诊断至关重要，然而诸如MedSAM之类的基础模型仍然是确定性的，并且在分布偏移下缺乏校准的不确定性。现有的保形预测方法提供了统计保证，但通常应用于2D且假设误差分布对称，因此无法捕捉3D多类分割中出现的类别特定偏差。我们提出类别感知非对称加权保形预测（CA-WCP），它将用于协变量偏移的潜在空间密度比加权与用于体积下界和上界的定向分位数相结合，并通过从验证集假阳性和假阴性率导出的类别特定非对称因子对每个边界进行缩放。我们证明CA-WCP对每个类别保持加权可交换边缘覆盖保证，并在3D脑肿瘤分割（BraTS 2020）以及在协变量偏移下构建的合成多器官CT基准上对其进行评估。在两个基准上，CA-WCP观测覆盖率的95\% Clopper--Pearson区间对每个语义类别都包含名义90\%水平，而区间宽度相对于对称加权保形预测减少了8--14\%。我们进一步将校准后的区间编码为结构化提示，输入多模态大语言模型以生成以不确定性为条件的放射学报告，从而将分布偏移感知的不确定性量化与可解释的临床沟通联系起来。
translation.title_zh: 量化体积风险：面向3D医学图像分割的类别感知非对称加权保形预测

paper.abstract: Generalized referring expression segmentation (GRES) requires dynamically balancing high-level semantics for identifying a variable number of language-specified referents with fine-grained visual evidence for precise boundary delineation. This requirement challenges existing cascaded vision-language architectures, which typically rely on static feature interfaces and single-pass mask prediction, limiting adaptive perception and geometric correction. We introduce ContourVLA, a vision-language-action policy that recasts GRES as a closed-loop visuomotor process, in which editable contours serve as explicit policy states that condition multimodal perception and are updated by geometric action chunks. Evolution-Aware Semantic Scheduling (EASS) couples contour-guided bidirectional boundary sampling with state-conditioned routing of multilevel multimodal features, adapting perception to each contour state. Following supervised initialization, Dustbin-Augmented Entropic Credit Transport GRPO (DECT-GRPO) jointly optimizes discrete grounding and continuous contour actions with instance-level credits. Its rollout rewards and credits are derived from soft prediction-target correspondences that account for false positives and missed targets. ContourVLA improves gIoU over the strongest evaluated baselines by 8.7, 2.8, and 2.7 points on gRefCOCO val, testA, and testB, respectively, and achieves the highest mIoU across all eight RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg splits.
paper.title: ContourVLA: A Closed-Loop Perception-Action Contour Policy for Generalized Referring Expression Segmentation

translation.abstract_zh: 广义指代表达分割（GRES）要求动态平衡用于识别可变数量语言指定指代对象的高层语义与用于精确边界描绘的细粒度视觉证据。这一需求对现有级联视觉-语言架构构成挑战，此类架构通常依赖静态特征接口和单次掩码预测，限制了自适应感知与几何校正。我们提出 ContourVLA，一种视觉-语言-动作策略，将 GRES 重构为闭环视觉运动过程，其中可编辑轮廓作为显式策略状态，条件化多模态感知并由几何动作块更新。演化感知语义调度（EASS）将轮廓引导的双向边界采样与状态条件化的多层级多模态特征路由相耦合，使感知适应每个轮廓状态。在监督初始化之后，Dustbin 增强熵信用传输 GRPO（DECT-GRPO）以实例级信用联合优化离散定位与连续轮廓动作。其 rollout 奖励与信用源自考虑误检和漏检目标的软预测-目标对应关系。ContourVLA 在 gRefCOCO val、testA 和 testB 上分别将 gIoU 较评估的最强基线提升 8.7、2.8 和 2.7 个点，并在全部八个 RefCOCO、RefCOCO+ 和 RefCOCOg 划分上取得最高 mIoU。
translation.title_zh: ContourVLA：面向广义指代表达分割的闭环感知-动作轮廓策略

paper.abstract: Modern machines can solve equations, follow logic and reason through language, yet they still struggle with problems that require visual non-verbal reasoning. This is evident even in advanced systems such as DeepSeek, ChatGPT and Gemini, which remain limited on visual tasks such as completing abstract patterns or delineating ambiguous regions-of-interest. Unlike explicit intermediate steps in verbal reasoning which can be verified through logic or automated tests, visual reasoning involves implicit intermediate steps with no clear methods for verification. Non-verbal reasoning is therefore challenging to model and, as a result, remains a fundamental limitation of current machine intelligence. Here we introduce GenVerOpt, a general framework that unifies generation, verification and optimisation into a reasoning pipeline for machines. By generating candidate solutions, verifying their correctness, and iteratively refining them, GenVerOpt enables per-sample optimisation rather than relying solely on dataset-level trends captured during model training. This process mirrors human problem-solving where multiple possibilities are imagined, evaluated, and refined until a correct solution emerges. Across diverse domains, GenVerOpt demonstrates capabilities beyond existing systems: it surpasses humans on abstract IQ puzzles, matches clinicians in prostate cancer segmentation, exceeds experts in liver vessel reconstruction and outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in tumour boundary alignment. These results show that machine reasoning can extend beyond language, establishing visual non-verbal reasoning as a foundation for more flexible and generalisable intelligence.
paper.title: Can machines reason non-verbally?

translation.abstract_zh: 现代机器能够解方程、遵循逻辑并通过语言进行推理，但它们在需要视觉非语言推理的问题上仍然举步维艰。这一点即使在DeepSeek、ChatGPT和Gemini等先进系统中也很明显，它们在完成抽象图案或勾画模糊感兴趣区域等视觉任务上仍然受限。与可以通过逻辑或自动化测试验证的语言推理中显式的中间步骤不同，视觉推理涉及隐式的中间步骤，且没有明确的验证方法。因此，非语言推理难以建模，并且因此仍然是当前机器智能的一个根本局限。在此，我们提出GenVerOpt，一个将生成、验证和优化统一为机器推理流程的通用框架。通过生成候选解、验证其正确性并迭代地改进它们，GenVerOpt实现了逐样本优化，而不是仅依赖模型训练期间捕获的数据集层面趋势。这一过程类似于人类解决问题的方式：想象多种可能性，对其进行评估并不断改进，直到出现正确解。在不同领域中，GenVerOpt展现出超越现有系统的能力：在抽象智商谜题上超越人类，在前列腺癌分割上匹配临床医生，在肝血管重建上超越专家，并在肿瘤边界对齐上优于最先进方法。这些结果表明，机器推理可以超越语言，确立视觉非语言推理作为更灵活、更具泛化能力的智能的基础。
translation.title_zh: 机器能进行非语言推理吗？

paper.abstract: Foundation models are increasingly used as feature extractors for downstream tasks with limited data, typically through representations obtained from their encoders. However, foundation models trained for structured tasks such as segmentation also form object-specific representations during task execution, whose transferability remains largely unexplored. We investigate Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) object pointers, compact object-level representations produced through the segmentation pathway, as transferable representations for downstream tumour prediction. Through experiments on two PET/CT tumour prediction tasks, we find that object pointers learned using segmentation supervision alone already encode tumour-discriminative information, despite never being optimised for the downstream labels. We further introduce task-guided object pointers, where an auxiliary objective jointly shapes the object pointer space for the downstream prediction together with segmentation. Task-guided pointers improve cancer-type classification, outperforming conventional encoder-based transfer and radiomics, while segmentation-only pointers perform best on the more challenging recurrence prediction task. Representation analyses reveal associations between object pointers and interpretable radiomics features, class-dependent organisation of the learned representation space, and explicit spatial grounding around the segmented tumour. Together, these findings suggest that useful transferable representations can emerge through the execution of a foundation model's primary task, providing an alternative to conventional encoder-based transfer.
paper.title: Beyond the Encoder: Object-Centric Representations Emerging from Segmentation Foundation Models

translation.abstract_zh: 基础模型越来越多地被用作数据有限的下游任务的特征提取器，通常通过从其编码器获得的表示来实现。然而，为分割等结构化任务训练的基础模型在执行任务期间也会形成对象特定的表示，其可迁移性在很大程度上仍未被探索。我们研究了Segment Anything Model 2（SAM2）对象指针——通过分割路径产生的紧凑对象级表示——作为下游肿瘤预测的可迁移表示。通过在两个PET/CT肿瘤预测任务上的实验，我们发现仅使用分割监督学习到的对象指针已经编码了肿瘤判别信息，尽管从未针对下游标签进行优化。我们进一步引入了任务引导的对象指针，其中辅助目标与分割一起共同塑造用于下游预测的对象指针空间。任务引导指针改善了癌症类型分类，优于传统的基于编码器的迁移和放射组学，而仅分割指针在更具挑战性的复发预测任务上表现最佳。表示分析揭示了对象指针与可解释放射组学特征之间的关联、所学表示空间的类别依赖性组织，以及围绕分割肿瘤的显式空间定位。总之，这些发现表明，有用的可迁移表示可以通过执行基础模型的主要任务而涌现，为传统的基于编码器的迁移提供了一种替代方案。
translation.title_zh: 超越编码器：从分割基础模型中涌现的对象中心表示

paper.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has been becoming a promising 3D reconstruction technique because of its advantage of high-fidelity rendering effect with high efficiency. However, it still suffers from coarse density control and semantically blind loss functions when reconstructing the fine-grained structures in complex urban scenes. Thus, this study proposes SG-GS, a semantic-guided 3DGS method for fine-grained structure reconstruction. It takes the semantic segmentation deduced by the Segment Anything Model (SAM) as a constraint and systematically integrates it into both Gaussian density control and loss function design. On the one hand, a semantic-constrained adaptive density control mechanism is constructed, which dynamically allocates gradient thresholds to different semantic regions of the scene and introduces an additional boundary-enhanced densification strategy, so that new Gaussians are directed to structurally critical regions. On the other hand, a multi-feature guided loss function is designed, and fine-grained supervision signals are gradually introduced through a phased progressive training strategy, alleviating the artifacts caused by the lack of semantic constraints in the basic loss. Experiments on three datasets show that the proposed method consistently improves reconstruction accuracy. Compared with the original 3DGS, the PSNR increases by approximately 2.7% to 5.2%, while artifacts on linear structures and boundary blurring are effectively mitigated. The method can serve the fine-grained 3D reconstruction of urban scenes.
paper.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Fine-grained Urban Scene Reconstruction via Semantic-guided Density Control and Loss Design

translation.abstract_zh: 3D高斯泼溅（3DGS）凭借其在高效率下实现高保真渲染效果的优势，正成为一种有前景的3D重建技术。然而，在重建复杂城市场景中的细粒度结构时，它仍然受制于粗糙的密度控制和语义盲的损失函数。因此，本研究提出SG-GS，一种用于细粒度结构重建的语义引导3DGS方法。它将由Segment Anything Model（SAM）推导出的语义分割作为约束，并系统性地将其融入高斯密度控制和损失函数设计中。一方面，构建了语义约束的自适应密度控制机制，该机制为场景的不同语义区域动态分配梯度阈值，并引入额外的边界增强致密化策略，从而将新高斯导向结构关键区域。另一方面，设计了多特征引导损失函数，并通过分阶段渐进训练策略逐步引入细粒度监督信号，缓解了基础损失中因缺乏语义约束而产生的伪影。在三个数据集上的实验表明，所提方法持续提升了重建精度。与原始3DGS相比，PSNR提高了约2.7%至5.2%，同时线性结构上的伪影和边界模糊得到了有效缓解。该方法可服务于城市场景的细粒度3D重建。
translation.title_zh: 基于语义引导密度控制与损失设计的3D高斯泼溅细粒度城市场景重建

paper.abstract: Specifying segmentation targets with natural language provides flexible semantic conditioning for medical image segmentation. However, existing methods still struggle to reliably ground high-level textual semantics into accurate pixel-level spatial prompts, especially under low-contrast lesions, ambiguous boundaries, and visually similar anatomical contexts. In this paper, we propose RADAR (Residual Aggregation and Dense Alignment Representations), a parameter-efficient framework for text-guided medical image segmentation. RADAR explicitly decouples and synergizes the medical semantic anchoring capability of BiomedCLIP with the prompt-driven mask decoding ability of MedSAM2, while enabling low-cost task adaptation via LoRA. Specifically, Guided Residual Depth Aggregation adaptively aggregates cross-layer features under semantic guidance to alleviate delayed textual injection and deep semantic dilution. Structured Dense Representation Alignment leverages a frozen BiomedCLIP to construct crop-level target, boundary, and context anchors, improving the local discriminability of dense features and the reliability of automatic prompts. Multi-modal Prompt Generation further converts cross-modal semantic responses into composite text, point, and mask prompts for MedSAM2 decoding. Experiments on three public medical image segmentation datasets show that RADAR achieves competitive performance with only 0.74M trainable parameters, demonstrating its effectiveness in parameter-efficient adaptation, semantic grounding, and dense representation enhancement. The source code is available at https://github.com/JGuiidev/RADAR.
paper.title: Text-Guided Medical Image Segmentation via Residual Aggregation and Dense Alignment Representations

translation.abstract_zh: 使用自然语言指定分割目标为医学图像分割提供了灵活的语义条件。然而，现有方法仍难以将高层文本语义可靠地落地为准确的像素级空间提示，尤其是在低对比度病灶、模糊边界和视觉相似的解剖上下文下。本文提出了 RADAR（残差聚合与稠密对齐表示），一种参数高效的文本引导医学图像分割框架。RADAR 显式解耦并协同 BiomedCLIP 的医学语义锚定能力与 MedSAM2 的提示驱动掩码解码能力，同时通过 LoRA 实现低成本的任务适应。具体而言，引导残差深度聚合在语义引导下自适应聚合跨层特征，以缓解文本注入延迟和深层语义稀释。结构化稠密表示对齐利用冻结的 BiomedCLIP 构建裁剪级目标、边界和上下文锚点，提高稠密特征的局部判别能力和自动提示的可靠性。多模态提示生成进一步将跨模态语义响应转换为复合文本、点和掩码提示，供 MedSAM2 解码。在三个公开医学图像分割数据集上的实验表明，RADAR 仅用 0.74M 可训练参数就取得了有竞争力的性能，证明了其在参数高效适应、语义落地和稠密表示增强方面的有效性。源代码可在 https://github.com/JGuiidev/RADAR 获取。
translation.title_zh: 基于残差聚合与稠密对齐表示的文本引导医学图像分割

paper.abstract: The recent Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3) extends powerful promptable segmentation from spatial cues to concepts, raising the prospect of a single foundation model for universal image segmentation. However, this promise often fails to translate into reliable performance on downstream segmentation tasks. In this work, we empirically identify concept recognition, rather than mask quality, as the primary bottleneck: SAM3 accurately delineates the objects it recognizes yet struggles to robustly determine which concepts are present. Driven by this, we present \textit{\underline{T}ext \underline{A}nchor re-\underline{G}rounding (\TAG{})}, a simple yet effective framework that rectifies the concept recognition of SAM3 on the target domain without dense annotations. Specifically, \TAG{} introduces an \textit{Anchor Residual Pathway} comprising image-conditioned, low-rank adapters to re-ground text anchors in the target distribution and modulate subsequent text-conditioned interactions. Guided solely by image-level category labels, \TAG{} jointly optimizes binary cross-entropy with \textit{Soft Boundary Ranking} objectives to calibrate presence confidence and distinguish present concepts from confusable negatives. Building upon this, we devise \textit{Confidence-Weighted Distillation} to couple rich semantic context of a multimodal large language model with fine-grained spatial priors of SAM3, thereby achieving effective calibration in the absence of manual annotations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that \TAG{} unlocks SAM3's segmentation potential with only 3.1M trainable parameters, achieving impressive performance across diverse scenarios, and notably, even surpassing leading mask-supervised methods on several metrics. \href{https://github.com/MiSsU-HH/TAG_SAM3}{Our code will be publicly available at GitHub \faGithub}.
paper.title: TAG: Calibrating SAM3 for Universal Image Segmentation without Dense Supervision

translation.abstract_zh: 最近的Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3) 将强大的可提示分割从空间线索扩展到概念，提升了单一基础模型用于通用图像分割的前景。然而，这一前景往往无法转化为在下游分割任务上的可靠性能。在本工作中，我们通过实证确定，概念识别而非掩码质量是主要瓶颈：SAM3能准确勾勒出其识别到的对象，却难以稳健地判断哪些概念存在。受此驱动，我们提出\textit{\underline{T}ext \underline{A}nchor re-\underline{G}rounding (\TAG{})}，一个简单而有效的框架，可在没有稠密标注的情况下校正SAM3在目标域上的概念识别。具体而言，\TAG{}引入\textit{Anchor Residual Pathway}，包含以图像为条件的低秩适配器，以在目标分布中重新定位文本锚点，并调制后续的文本条件交互。仅由图像级类别标签引导，\TAG{}联合优化二元交叉熵与\textit{Soft Boundary Ranking}目标，以校准存在置信度并区分存在概念与易混淆负样本。在此基础上，我们设计\textit{Confidence-Weighted Distillation}，将多模态大语言模型丰富的语义上下文与SAM3细粒度的空间先验耦合，从而在缺乏人工标注的情况下实现有效校准。大量实验表明，\TAG{}仅用3.1M可训练参数就释放了SAM3的分割潜力，在多样场景中取得令人印象深刻的性能，并且值得注意的是，在若干指标上甚至超越了领先的掩码监督方法。\href{https://github.com/MiSsU-HH/TAG_SAM3}{我们的代码将在GitHub上公开：\faGithub}。
translation.title_zh: TAG：无需稠密监督校准SAM3以实现通用图像分割

paper.abstract: Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) is a foundation model for image and video segmentation that sets the state of the art in visual object tracking. Its tracker, inherited from SAM 2, stores information from past frames in a memory bank, managed by a simple First-In-First-Out rule, allowing temporal consistency in complex videos. Several recent methods improve SAM 2 with hand-crafted memory update rules, each targeting a specific failure mode, such as distractors, occlusions, or object motion. However, their gains transfer only partially to the stronger SAM 3 backbone. We instead present a more general, data-driven approach that frames memory control as a sequential decision-making task. SAM3RL is an extension of the SAM 3 tracker with a lightweight memory controller, trained by reinforcement learning, that decides which frames enter the memory bank in order to maximize tracking performance. SAM3RL sets a new state of the art on 10 of 12 tracking and video object segmentation benchmarks, outperforming all hand-crafted rules without any runtime overhead. The same approach applied to SAM 2 gives SAM2RL, which outperforms hand-crafted rules on 9 of the 12 benchmarks, showing the generality of our method across model generations.
paper.title: SAM3RL: Memory Control via Reinforcement Learning for Visual Object Tracking

translation.abstract_zh: Segment Anything Model 3（SAM 3）是一种用于图像和视频分割的基础模型，在视觉目标跟踪中达到了当前最优性能。其跟踪器继承自 SAM 2，将过去帧的信息存储在记忆库中，并由简单的先进先出规则管理，从而在复杂视频中实现时间一致性。近期若干方法通过手工设计的记忆更新规则改进 SAM 2，每种规则针对特定的失败模式，如干扰物、遮挡或目标运动。然而，它们的增益只能部分迁移到更强的 SAM 3 骨干上。我们转而提出一种更通用、数据驱动的方法，将记忆控制建模为序贯决策任务。SAM3RL 是 SAM 3 跟踪器的扩展，带有一个轻量级记忆控制器，通过强化学习训练，决定哪些帧进入记忆库以最大化跟踪性能。SAM3RL 在 12 个跟踪和视频目标分割基准中的 10 个上创造了新的当前最优性能，在没有任何运行时开销的情况下优于所有手工设计的规则。将同一方法应用于 SAM 2 得到 SAM2RL，其在 12 个基准中的 9 个上优于手工设计的规则，表明我们的方法在不同模型代际间具有通用性。
translation.title_zh: SAM3RL：基于强化学习的视觉目标跟踪记忆控制

paper.abstract: Spatial agents have access to reconstruction and segmentation tools, yet inconsistent predictions and fragmented object identities can prevent their outputs from becoming reliable 3D scene information. A simple oracle experiment exposes this perception bottleneck: replacing tool-predicted perception with ground-truth 3D bounding boxes raises an agent to nearly full score across five object-centric VSI-Bench tasks, while retaining the same reasoning tools. Motivated by this finding, we believe the devil of spatial reasoning lies in 3D itself, and introduce DeSpatial(Devil of Spatial), which explicitly decomposes spatial understanding into perception and reasoning. DeSpatial has a shared 3D perception tool to reconcile independent perception outputs into a unified, metric, gravity-aligned 3D scene. This perception tool has two core components: a) a joint segmentation--depth co-refinement module that consolidates masks of the same object and removes projection artifacts caused by inconsistent segmentation and depth within a single frame; b) a cross-view instance fusion module that consolidate voxel-overlapping instances but not allowed to merge same-frame instances. This fusion module additionally fuses spatially disjoint fragments caused by insufficient multi-view observations, by checking their 3D structure and source mask appearance. After receiving the complete and unified 3D scene information, the agent chooses reasoning or computational tools to solve the spatial problem. DeSpatial achieves leading performance on VSI-Bench, MindCube-Tiny, and ViewSpatial, with additional long-video results on VSI-SUPER, revealing the bottleneck of spatial understanding lies in a precise 3D perception itself.
paper.title: DeSpatial: The devil of Agentic Spatial Reasoning Lies in 3D Itself

translation.abstract_zh: 空间智能体可以使用重建与分割工具，但不一致的预测和碎片化的对象身份会阻碍其输出成为可靠的3D场景信息。一个简单的oracle实验揭示了这一感知瓶颈：在五个以对象为中心的VSI-Bench任务上，将工具预测的感知替换为真值3D边界框后，智能体在保留相同推理工具的情况下得分接近满分。受此发现启发，我们认为空间推理的魔鬼藏在3D本身之中，并提出了DeSpatial（Devil of Spatial），它将空间理解显式分解为感知与推理。DeSpatial有一个共享的3D感知工具，将独立的感知输出协调为一个统一的、度量的、重力对齐的3D场景。该感知工具包含两个核心组件：a）一个联合分割--深度协同细化模块，用于合并同一对象的面具，并消除单帧内因分割与深度不一致导致的投影伪影；b）一个跨视角实例融合模块，用于合并体素重叠的实例，但不允许合并同一帧内的实例。该融合模块还通过检查空间上不相交碎片（由多视角观测不足导致）的3D结构和源面具外观来进一步融合它们。在接收到完整且统一的3D场景信息后，智能体选择推理或计算工具来解决空间问题。DeSpatial在VSI-Bench、MindCube-Tiny和ViewSpatial上取得了领先性能，并在VSI-SUPER上给出了额外的长视频结果，揭示空间理解的瓶颈在于精确的3D感知本身。
translation.title_zh: DeSpatial：具身空间推理的魔鬼藏在3D本身之中

paper.abstract: Reasoning Video Object Segmentation (RVOS) aims to localize and segment objects referred to by natural-language expressions throughout a video. Although large vision-language models (LVLMs) implicitly encode localization cues in their attention maps, these attentions are often noisy, diffuse, and scattered across layers, heads, and modalities, limiting their direct use for segmentation. Existing methods typically rely on handcrafted attention-selection heuristics or computationally expensive attention refinement. We propose ATLAS, an attention adaptation framework that learns to transform raw LVLM attentions into object-centric localization cues. ATLAS treats attentions from all layers, heads, and modalities as structured features, combining high-resolution frame-level attentions that capture spatial information with low-resolution video-level attentions that encode temporal context. A lightweight U-Net equipped with temporal attention and FiLM-based modulation fuses these complementary representations to generate coarse segmentation heatmaps, which are propagated across the video using SAM2. Extensive experiments on challenging referring and reasoning video segmentation benchmarks show that ATLAS outperforms existing frozen-backbone methods. Code and models are available at \url{https://hamidreza-136.github.io/atlas/}.
paper.title: ATLAS: Learning to Adapt LVLM Attention for Reasoning Video Segmentation

translation.abstract_zh: 推理视频目标分割（RVOS）旨在定位并分割视频中由自然语言表达所指代的对象。尽管大型视觉语言模型（LVLM）在其注意力图中隐式编码了定位线索，但这些注意力往往噪声大、分散，并散落在不同层、头和模态之间，限制了它们直接用于分割。现有方法通常依赖手工设计的注意力选择启发式规则或计算昂贵的注意力细化。我们提出 ATLAS，一个注意力适配框架，学习将原始 LVLM 注意力转换为以对象为中心的定位线索。ATLAS 将所有层、头和模态的注意力视为结构化特征，将捕获空间信息的高分辨率帧级注意力与编码时间上下文的低分辨率视频级注意力相结合。一个配备时间注意力和基于 FiLM 的调制的轻量级 U-Net 融合这些互补表示以生成粗分割热图，并通过 SAM2 在视频中传播。在具有挑战性的指代和推理视频分割基准上的大量实验表明，ATLAS 优于现有的冻结骨干方法。代码和模型可在 \url{https://hamidreza-136.github.io/atlas/} 获取。
translation.title_zh: ATLAS：学习适配 LVLM 注意力以实现推理视频分割

paper.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have significantly advanced instruction-driven perception through the "Embedding-as-Mask" paradigm. However, extending this capability to Remote Sensing (RS) reasoning segmentation remains exceptionally challenging under cluttered geographical contexts and extreme scale variations, often leading to Spatial Fidelity Degradation and Target Misidentification. We identify a critical yet underexplored bottleneck: the sequential alienation of the segmentation token [SEG] from its initial visual grounding within the autoregressive generation paradigm. Produced only at the end of long reasoning chains, [SEG] relies on visual evidence that has been progressively diluted by linguistic abstraction and autoregressive noise. This information decay is particularly catastrophic for RS targets with minuscule pixel footprints, where even marginal fidelity loss leads to localization failure. To address these bottlenecks, we propose GeoReason, a novel framework designed to fortify logical deduction and preserve spatial integrity. First, we introduce an Anticipatory Prior mechanism that injects the [SEG] token directly into the initial user query, shifting it from a terminal output to a primary condition. This paradigm shift transforms the token into a persistent spatial anchor, preventing information decay during long-form linguistic inference. Second, we enhance visual reasoning via a Location-aware Chain-of-Thought (CoT) that enforces coarse-to-fine localization using bounding boxes, coupled with a Latent Patch-to-Token Alignment (PTA) Loss that explicitly aligns the latent segmentation token with physical RS textures. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GeoReason consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on the Earthreason and RRSIS-D benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/Fanc0126/GeoReason.
paper.title: GeoReason: Bridging Logical Reasoning and Spatial Fidelity in Remote Sensing Segmentation

paper.abstract:
Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) answer questions about whole images well, yet they still struggle with fine-grained region understanding. A key reason is that text-only supervision never specifies which regions support an answer. To close this gap, we present Xiaomi-Lens-0, a 4B MLLM built on Qwen3.5 that predicts masks from its own visual representations. Specifically, a lightweight decoder combines vision-encoder patch features with the language model's mask-token states, termed visual latents, so that mask supervision reaches the shared backbone without an additional segmentation encoder. Because each latent decodes to a mask, the model can interleave reasoning with region-specific latents and thus think with visual latents, while grounded reasoning traces supervise the intermediate regions referenced during chain-of-thought. As a result, across all eight RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg splits, Xiaomi-Lens-0 gains 5.6 points on average over Qwen3.5 in referring comprehension and achieves the highest segmentation cIoU among compared models. Moreover, it surpasses Qwen3.5 across all perception benchmarks.

decision.reason: Abstract describes an unsupervised general-image SAM pretraining framework using motion pseudo-labels and contrastive learning. It does not address medical imaging, reasoning segmentation, implicit/spatial reasoning to pixel masks, or RL/DPO methods. It also is not a traditional segmentation/SAM loss or optimization objective with theoretical grounding and transfer evidence to the stated medical/reasoning tasks; the transferable_objective rule hit appears to come from generic "transferable objectness prior" wording.

paper.abstract: The Segment Anything Model (SAM) relies heavily on massive manual annotations, creating a fundamental bottleneck for model scaling. While unsupervised methods attempt to learn object concepts from motion, they typically overfit to moving entities, lacking both multi-granularity understanding and the ability to generalize to static objects. To overcome this, we introduce Motion-Grounded Segment Anything (MoSA), a highly scalable unsupervised framework that learns a transferable objectness prior from unlabeled videos. MoSA operates in three progressive stages: (1) automatically generating multi-granularity motion pseudo-labels from large-scale video data; (2) training a Perceptual Grouping Model (PGM) via contrastive learning to internalize a generalized, appearance-driven concept of objects; and (3) transferring this learned prior into a prompt-guided architecture for segment-anything-style inference on images. Extensive zero-shot evaluations across seven challenging benchmarks (e.g., COCO and ADE20K) demonstrate that MoSA significantly outperforms existing unsupervised methods. Notably, despite using zero manual annotations, MoSA achieves segmentation performance comparable to the fully supervised SAM. Our findings reveal that harnessing large-scale unlabeled motion is a feasible and highly scalable alternative to annotation-driven segment-anything pipelines.
paper.title: Seeing as Humans Do: Learning from Motion to Segment Anything Without Supervision

We introduce PixelDense, which routes DINOv2 and SAM2 through a semantic projection stream, routes Depth Anything v2 and Metric3D v2 through a geometric projection stream, and adds a weight-space orthogonality penalty that keeps the two streams in disjoint subspaces.

Applied to PixelGen and DeCo with a single recipe, PixelDense improves GenEval, DPG-Bench, and HPS v2.1, raises PixelGen-XXL's GenEval Overall from 0.7927 to 0.8093, and beats every single-teacher and unfactored multi-teacher variant.

It does not address medical reasoning segmentation, spatial/position reasoning to pixel masks, DPO, or RL. The weight-space orthogonality penalty is a diffusion-training objective, and the abstract provides no theory or transfer evidence for medical mask reasoning. Thus the SAM2/dense-prediction keyword hit does not indicate a substantive contribution to the target interests.

paper.abstract: Representation alignment (REPA) accelerates diffusion transformer training, but its alignment targets are almost exclusively semantic encoders such as DINOv2 and CLIP. Recent analysis points to spatial structure, not global semantics, as the carrier of the alignment effect, yet dense-prediction foundation models trained to predict that structure remain overlooked as REPA targets. In pixel-space diffusion, SAM2, Depth Anything v2, and Metric3D v2 each outperform the DINOv2-only GenEval baseline, with the two geometric teachers leading the segmentation teacher. A flat sum of all four teachers, however, lands below the best single geometric teacher, as semantic and geometric gradients compete for one denoiser projection. We introduce PixelDense, which routes DINOv2 and SAM2 through a semantic projection stream, routes Depth Anything v2 and Metric3D v2 through a geometric projection stream, and adds a weight-space orthogonality penalty that keeps the two streams in disjoint subspaces. All four teachers are frozen during training and dropped at inference. Applied to PixelGen and DeCo with a single recipe, PixelDense improves GenEval, DPG-Bench, and HPS v2.1, raises PixelGen-XXL's GenEval Overall from 0.7927 to 0.8093, and beats every single-teacher and unfactored multi-teacher variant. In partial-noise reconstruction, independent panoptic, depth, and surface-normal probes show up to 53.1% PQ gain and 36.0% depth AbsRel reduction at $τ=0.5$ across COCO and Flickr30K. From random initialization, PixelDense also reaches the baseline's peak GenEval 1.23x faster. In SDEdit editing on PIE-Bench, PixelDense keeps more of the source background and layout at every edit strength, raising background PSNR by up to 2.2 dB.
paper.title: PixelDense: Dense Prediction as Representation Alignment for Pixel Diffusion

paper.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have emerged as powerful candidates for universal vision backbones, with representative architectures including autoregressive (AR) models and diffusion transformers (DiTs). Yet, adapting them efficiently for all-in-one low-level image restoration remains a challenge. Crucially, the field lacks an understanding of how VLMs organize hidden-layer representations and whether these structurally distinct paradigms share a common geometric organization for pixel-level perception. Such shared organization is a prerequisite for building highly transferable, unified restoration VLMs and adapters. In this paper, we systematically investigate representational similarity across 24 low-level tasks spanning 5 categories. We propose GeoSim, a unified four-level framework that analyzes task-conditioned representations from global similarity, local geometry, sparse feature decomposition, and topological verification perspectives. Our formulation applies to the analysis of hidden states in AR models and feature maps in DiTs across same- and cross-task/model settings. Our results reveal the organizing principles of low-level visual representations while exposing their limits in cross-task and cross-model agreement. Ultimately, GeoSim provides an interpretability lens for probing latent transferability in low-level vision and diagnosing model limitations in task- or model-specific scenarios.
paper.title: Geometric Similarity in VLM Low-Level Vision Representations

CineMR is trained with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on tool-interaction traces followed by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with conditional tool-use rewards.
Correct tool invocation reaches 99.8% after GRPO, up from 78.9% after SFT.

It is relevant to medical reasoning with RL, but the task is quantitative CMR assessment and tool-integrated VQA, not reasoning segmentation to pixel masks; segmentation tools are auxiliary. paper.abstract: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR), including cine imaging, is a reference standard for the noninvasive assessment of cardiac morphology and ventricular function. Cine CMR interpretation integrates qualitative visual assessment with quantitative measurements of ventricular volumes, ejection fraction, myocardial mass, wall thickness, and regional wall motion. Current medical vision-language models (VLMs) cannot reliably derive quantitative measurements from multidimensional cine images without analysis tools. We present CineMR, a tool-augmented VLM that invokes cardiac image-analysis tools and integrates their outputs into interleaved reasoning for quantitative CMR assessment. We also construct a multi-cohort visual question answering benchmark covering quantitative metric extraction, multiclass diagnosis, and differential diagnosis, together with tools for segmentation, phase selection, volumetry, morphometry, and regional wall motion analysis. CineMR is trained with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on tool-interaction traces followed by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with conditional tool-use rewards. On the multi-cohort cine CMR benchmark, CineMR achieves 35.9% pass@1 and 58.9% pass@4, compared with 1.5% pass@1 for the Qwen3-VL-8B backbone and 0.0% and 7.0% pass@1 for LLaVA-Med v1.5 and MedGemma-4B, respectively. Correct tool invocation reaches 99.8% after GRPO, up from 78.9% after SFT. Live tool outputs improve ventricular measurement accuracy by 20.4--23.7% over direct model predictions, and removing all tools reduces pass@1 from 35.9% to 27.9%. These results highlight the importance of reliable tool use for quantitative cine CMR reasoning and support CineMR as a promising approach for assistive cardiac image assessment. Code, benchmark resources, and model weights are available at https://github.com/AI-MIND-Lab/CineMR.
paper.title: CineMR: Tool-Integrated Vision-Language Reasoning for Quantitative Cardiac MRI Assessment

We further adopt vision-language models (VLM) to automatically generate scene-specific semantic prompts for SAM 3, enabling precise instance-level segmentation that distinguishes which objects move from what objects exist.

paper.abstract: Recent depth foundation models like Depth Anything 3 (DA3) achieve remarkable multi-view depth estimation but assume static 3D scenes, limiting their applicability to real-world dynamic environments. Existing training-free 4D methods like Easi3R and VGGT4D rely on correspondence-trained backbones whose attention encodes cross-frame matching, a property absent in depth-only models like DA3. We present Dyna3, a training-free framework that extends DA3 for 4D dynamic scene reconstruction without any fine-tuning. Our key insight is that DA3's cross-view features, though trained only for depth consistency, implicitly encode motion-discriminative signals when combined with best-match feature search across frames. Its static surfaces find consistent matches globally, while dynamic objects cannot. We further adopt vision-language models (VLM) to automatically generate scene-specific semantic prompts for SAM 3, enabling precise instance-level segmentation that distinguishes which objects move from what objects exist. For reconstruction, we decouple the scene into a cross-frame aligned static background and per-frame dynamic point clouds. Experiments on four datasets demonstrate that Dyna3 surpasses correspondence-trained methods with +5.5pp J-Mean over state-of-the-art VGGT4D on dynamic object segmentation, while achieving up to 13x faster pose estimation and 3x faster 4D reconstruction with 4 to 8x lower memory. Dyna3 could therefore enable much denser temporal sampling that prior methods cannot support.
paper.title: Dyna3: VLM-Guided Training-Free 4D Reconstruction via Depth Foundation Models

paper.abstract: Automatic horizon tracking is a foundational task in 3D seismic interpretation. Most existing deep learning approaches formulate it as dense semantic segmentation, typically using U-Net-based architectures. The model produces a probability map over all pixels that must be post-processed to extract precise horizon coordinates, while horizon picks in time/depth must be converted into dense masks for training. Unpicked seismic traces are consequently treated as background, which can hinder convergence, and both pre- and post-processing can introduce errors into the final interpretation. Moreover, 2D segmentation models do not inherently capture inter-slice context, while 3D models are often computationally prohibitive. We instead formulate horizon tracking as a bounded coordinate regression problem, where the model directly predicts the time/depth coordinate of the target horizon at each lateral position. We propose a lightweight regression head compatible with any pretrained vision backbone, coupled with an LSTM module to model inter-slice context and produce a continuous horizon surface across the volume. A combination of L1 and L2 losses supervises predictions at valid horizon picks, while a geology-informed regularization enforces lateral continuity between successive traces. Under controlled experimental conditions, we evaluate four pretrained vision backbones under both segmentation and regression configurations on a seismic volume from New Zealand. The proposed approach consistently outperforms its segmentation counterparts quantitatively, using metrics including RMSE and PCC, and qualitatively, while also demonstrating greater robustness to increasing sparsity of training picks. Finally, we show that prediction variation across successive traces captures local variations in geological complexity, providing an automated quality control measure for downstream seismic interpretation.
paper.title: DeepStratNet: A Context-Aware Coordinate Regression Framework for Seismic Horizon Tracking under Sparse Labels

translation.abstract_zh: 自动层位追踪是三维地震解释中的一项基础任务。大多数现有深度学习方法将其表述为密集语义分割，通常使用基于U-Net的架构。该模型在所有像素上产生概率图，必须经过后处理才能提取精确的层位坐标，而时间/深度上的层位拾取必须转换为密集掩码以进行训练。因此，未拾取的地震道被视为背景，这可能阻碍收敛，并且预处理和后处理都可能给最终解释引入误差。此外，二维分割模型本质上无法捕捉切片间上下文，而三维模型通常在计算上难以承受。我们转而将层位追踪表述为有界坐标回归问题，其中模型直接预测每个横向位置上目标层位的时间/深度坐标。我们提出了一种轻量级回归头，可与任何预训练视觉骨干网络兼容，并结合LSTM模块来建模切片间上下文，从而在整个数据体上生成连续的层位表面。L1和L2损失的组合在有效层位拾取处监督预测，而地质信息正则化则强制连续道之间的横向连续性。在受控实验条件下，我们在来自新西兰的一个地震数据体上，评估了四种预训练视觉骨干网络在分割和回归配置下的表现。所提出的方法在定量指标（包括RMSE和PCC）和定性方面均持续优于其分割对应方法，同时还表现出对训练拾取稀疏性增加的更强鲁棒性。最后，我们表明连续道之间的预测变化捕捉了地质复杂性的局部变化，为下游地震解释提供了一种自动质量控制措施。

paper.abstract: Video Object Segmentation (VOS) in complex and long videos is increasingly important for real-world applications, where target objects often appear only intermittently within long temporal horizons. However, existing benchmarks largely focus on temporally salient objects that remain visible for most of the video. To address this gap, we introduce FaVOS (A Benchmark for Video Object Segmentation with Fractional Temporal Visibility), a benchmark designed to evaluate VOS methods under low temporal visibility. We show that, in this regime, the standard J&F metric can collapse VOS evaluation into absence classification, because empty predictions receive high rewards on target-absent frames. Consequently, even a trivial empty-mask predictor can outperform strong models such as SAM 3, revealing a fundamental mismatch between current metrics and practical VOS performance. To mitigate this issue, we propose Volumetric J&F, which evaluates mask sequences as spatio-temporal volumes and reduces the dominance of target-absence rewards while preserving sensitivity to segmentation quality and temporal structure. Project page: https://aidaslab.github.io/FaVOS.
paper.title: When Predicting Nothing Beats SAM 3: Revisiting Evaluation in Video Object Segmentation

abstract_evidence: Accurate three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction of individual dendrites in serial block-face scanning electron microscopy (SBF-SEM) is essential for quantifying structural plasticity in the brain, yet manual annotation at scale is infeasible.

paper.abstract: Editable 3D models of field-grown crops support high-throughput phenotyping and in silico breeding trials, but building them from scanned point clouds requires organ-level segmentation and fitting. Procedural generators can turn an organ-level parameter set into an analysis-suitable 3D model, but obtaining that set requires hours of manual tuning per plant or segmentation models trained on species-specific labels. We present an automated pipeline that reconstructs procedural maize models from raw 3D point clouds without manual tuning or species-specific training data. A multimodal vision-language model (VLM) annotates leaf midlines in rendered orthographic views. Deterministic geometric algorithms back-project the annotations onto the point cloud, merge them into 3D leaves by cross-view consensus, and grow the midlines to full blades on an orientation-weighted surface graph. Measured organ parameters populate a plant descriptor for a Non-Uniform Rational B-Spline (NURBS)-based procedural model generator. Each leaf surface is then refined against its scan points by differentiable NURBS fitting. The pipeline reached a median whole-plant Chamfer distance of 5.4 mm on 100 genotypically diverse field-grown maize plants from the MaizeField3D dataset. The reconstructions were closer to the scans than those of an earlier semi-automated pipeline based on manual annotations. The pipeline recovered 1,017 of 1,023 (99.4%) curated reference leaves at an intersection-over-union of at least 0.5 without using those labels as input. These results show that VLM annotations become usable organ-level measurements when downstream geometric stages can correct them. This makes automated generation of editable 3D plant assets feasible at the scale of modern phenotyping experiments.
paper.title: A Vision-Language Model (VLM)-based Pipeline for End-to-End Procedural Modeling of Field-Grown Maize from Point Clouds

paper.abstract: Visual grounding models can enhance radiology workflows by linking report findings to image regions. This is particularly valuable for 3D CT, where findings often occupy a tiny fraction of the volume. Training 3D grounding models requires large sets of paired phrases and regions, and building such datasets is expensive, requiring radiologists to annotate images by hand. We posit that this supervision is already created implicitly during routine reporting, as radiologists frequently place 2D annotations (e.g., distance measurement, arrows) on key images to make measurements and to support report interpretation. We introduce an automated pipeline that converts these routine clinical annotations into large-scale phrase-region supervision for 3D visual grounding. The pipeline links each annotation to the corresponding finding in the report through metadata matching, then uses a promptable 3D segmentation model to convert the 2D annotation into a volumetric mask. This produces phrase-mask-volume datasets without requiring additional radiologist annotation. Applied to a single institution's clinical picture archiving and communication system (PACS), our approach generated 105K phrase-mask-volume triplets from 59K abdominal CT exams. We also introduce two abdominal CT grounding benchmarks, LocusBench-Onc and LocusBench-ED, which comprise 240 oncology and 260 emergency-department radiologist-reviewed phrase-mask-volume triplets, respectively, with the latter spanning 13 distinct categories such as appendicitis, hematoma, and hernia. We further introduce LocusCT, a 3D visual grounding model trained on this dataset, which achieves hit rates of 0.725 on LocusBench-Onc and 0.773 on LocusBench-ED, substantially outperforming comparator models. These results show that routine PACS annotations are a scalable, previously unused source of supervision for 3D visual grounding.
paper.title: Scaling 3D Visual Grounding in Abdominal CT

paper.abstract: Bird monitoring in natural environments is challenging due to the small size of some species of birds relative to the scene, background clutter, variability in illumination, and the observers' viewpoint. Progress is further limited by the scarcity of large-scale, realistic datasets, which are essential for understanding behavioral patterns. To address this gap, we introduce a new benchmark dataset for the detection and segmentation of Western bluebirds (Sialia Mexicana), comprising over 6,000 labeled images from 41 recording sessions. The dataset features high-resolution (4K) in-the-wild images in which birds occupy only a small fraction of the image. We evaluated supervised detectors, open-vocabulary models under zero-shot and fine-tuned settings, and segmentation approaches. Supervised detectors remain the most reliable overall, with Faster R-CNN achieving the highest detection mAP and RT-DETR offering the best precision-recall trade-off. Open-vocabulary models perform poorly in zero-shot settings; however, fine-tuning substantially improves their performance, with YOLO-World becoming competitive with supervised methods and achieving the highest precision, F1-score, and mAP@0.5. For segmentation, supervised methods significantly outperform Grounded-SAM and SAM 3: Mask R-CNN achieves the highest mask mAP, while YOLOv8-Seg provides the best precision and fastest inference. A diagnostic analysis further shows that failures are not explained by object size alone, but by a combination of apparent scale, brightness, contrast, clutter, blur, crowding, and recording-session variation. Overall, our findings highlight the difficulty of zero-shot bird detection in cluttered ecological scenes and underscore the importance of domain adaptation in small-object settings.
paper.title: Towards benchmarking Western Bluebird detection in the wild

paper.abstract: Reliable volumetric segmentation is critical for clinical diagnostics, yet foundation models such as MedSAM remain deterministic and lack calibrated uncertainty under distribution shift. Existing conformal prediction methods offer statistical guarantees but are frequently applied in 2D and assume symmetric error distributions, so they do not capture the class-specific biases that arise in 3D multi-class segmentation. We propose Class-Aware Asymmetric Weighted Conformal Prediction (CA-WCP), which combines latent-space density-ratio weighting for covariate shift with directional quantiles for the lower and upper volume bounds, and scales each bound by a class-specific asymmetry factor derived from validation-set false-positive and false-negative rates. We prove that CA-WCP retains the weighted-exchangeability marginal coverage guarantee for every class, and we evaluate it on 3D brain tumor segmentation (BraTS 2020) and on a synthetic multi-organ CT benchmark constructed under covariate shift. On both benchmarks the 95\% Clopper--Pearson interval for the observed coverage of CA-WCP contains the nominal 90\% level for every semantic class, while interval width is reduced by 8--14\% relative to symmetric weighted conformal prediction. We further encode the calibrated intervals into structured prompts for a multimodal large language model to produce uncertainty-conditioned radiology reports, linking distribution-shift-aware uncertainty quantification to interpretable clinical communication.
paper.title: Quantifying Volumetric Risk: Class-Aware Asymmetric Weighted Conformal Prediction for 3D Medical Image Segmentation

paper.abstract: Referring Expression Segmentation (RES) links natural-language descriptions to pixel-level object masks. Yet standard evaluation provides limited insight into instance-level referential reasoning: it does not systematically distinguish referential logics, test target preservation across valid grounding paths, or separate target-selection from mask-generation errors. We introduce InstanceBench, an instance-centered diagnostic benchmark comprising 6,194 images, 9,264 target instances, and 25,077 human-verified expressions. Each target-centric expression set (TCES) fixes the image and target mask while pairing a minimal expression with a same-target variant that uses another valid cue or grounding path. A compact referential-logic taxonomy spans direct target evidence, same-class selection, relational and compositional grounding, and exclusion, while logic-critical construction suppresses simpler shortcuts. Identity-aware metrics measure target retention and set-level success while separating selection from mask-generation errors. Across 22 native-mask RES checkpoints from 18 model families, the strongest checkpoint reaches 67.1% mIoU but only 59.6% All@0.7. Controlled interventions confirm language sensitivity, while failure decomposition identifies target selection rather than mask decoding as the main bottleneck. On a controlled training subset, matched supervision improves identity-aware performance, showing that the diagnosed capability responds to targeted supervision. Collectively, InstanceBench supports a measure-diagnose-improve cycle: measuring target consistency across grounding paths, localizing failure sources, and evaluating targeted interventions.
paper.title: InstanceBench: Diagnosing Referential Reasoning and Target Identity in Referring Expression Segmentation

paper.abstract: Generalized referring expression segmentation (GRES) requires dynamically balancing high-level semantics for identifying a variable number of language-specified referents with fine-grained visual evidence for precise boundary delineation. This requirement challenges existing cascaded vision-language architectures, which typically rely on static feature interfaces and single-pass mask prediction, limiting adaptive perception and geometric correction. We introduce ContourVLA, a vision-language-action policy that recasts GRES as a closed-loop visuomotor process, in which editable contours serve as explicit policy states that condition multimodal perception and are updated by geometric action chunks. Evolution-Aware Semantic Scheduling (EASS) couples contour-guided bidirectional boundary sampling with state-conditioned routing of multilevel multimodal features, adapting perception to each contour state. Following supervised initialization, Dustbin-Augmented Entropic Credit Transport GRPO (DECT-GRPO) jointly optimizes discrete grounding and continuous contour actions with instance-level credits. Its rollout rewards and credits are derived from soft prediction-target correspondences that account for false positives and missed targets. ContourVLA improves gIoU over the strongest evaluated baselines by 8.7, 2.8, and 2.7 points on gRefCOCO val, testA, and testB, respectively, and achieves the highest mIoU across all eight RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg splits.
paper.title: ContourVLA: A Closed-Loop Perception-Action Contour Policy for Generalized Referring Expression Segmentation

paper.abstract: Current stereo vision-based approaches for food portion estimation are hindered by the user burden of using a mobile phone to capture multiple images or placing a reference object in the scene for scale calibration. As a step towards passive dietary intake monitoring, we introduce a method that uses stereo video from a wearable egocentric device to reconstruct food items in true physical scale to accurately estimate volume. By utilizing FoundationStereo for zero-shot stereo matching, SAM 2 for food segmentation, and TSDF fusion over a set of keyframes, our method yields a visually and metrically accurate 3D mesh of any plated food item from a single stereo recording. We leverage the unique offerings of wearables, such as a factory-calibrated stereo baseline and camera poses estimated on-device via visual-inertial odometry (VIO), to perform fully automatic reconstruction without a scale reference object in the scene. We show strong initial volume estimation results across five recorded food items, achieving a mean absolute percentage error of 9.1%.
paper.title: Reference-Free Food Volume Estimation from Egocentric Stereo Video

paper.abstract: 3D reconstruction of building components using image-based scanning requires appropriate segmentation of the objects in the 2D building images. In order to benefit from consistent grouping of the 2D masks in 3D environments, vision foundation models such as the Segment Anything Model have been utilized by Group Anything with Radiance Fields (GARField) to perform 3D segmentation. This study fine-tuned SAM 2.1 on the HBD dataset, consisting of 2,679 annotated images from 42 buildings, to enhance multi-class segmentation of 2D building images, covering 11 classes (Wall, Window, Ceiling, Door, Column, Beam, Floor, Opening, Curtain Wall, Roof, and Lift). The model was evaluated using per-class IoU, Dice, and mIoU metrics, and the results show an improvement in mIoU from 49.9% to 69.6%, indicating a meaningful improvement in class segmentation and providing a more accurate model for distilling the masks in 3D. SegFormer was then used as a baseline, generating per-class masks for comparison with SAM 2.1, which indicates improvement in some object classes with larger surface area. The masks in the building images were grouped in the neural radiance field, and the pretrained SAM 2.1 was compared with the fine-tuned SAM 2.1 in the newly rendered images. This comparison shows that fine-tuning improves the grouping of building components at a user-selected grouping scale. This advances the application of Group Anything with Radiance Fields (GARField) in 3D, enabling better segmentation of building structures for 3D auto-reconstruction.
paper.title: Domain Adaptation of SAM 2.1 for Building-Component Segmentation in Image-Based 3D Reconstruction

It does not describe reasoning segmentation, implicit-request or spatial/position reasoning to pixel masks, DPO/RL, or a theory-backed transferable segmentation optimization objective. paper.abstract: Recent advances in large-scale foundation models have enabled strong generalization across a wide range of clinical and research tasks in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). However, existing vision-language MRI models remain limited in anatomy-specific localization and pathology-aware representation, particularly in real-world settings. We introduce A4-MR, a 3D vision-language foundation model trained on approximately 50,000 MRI studies comprising 491,000 series, roughly half of which are paired with radiology reports. A4-MR is designed to: (1) learn anatomy localization through large-scale pretraining with noisy labels; (2) align image and text representations at the anatomical level; and (3) learn distinct representations of healthy and abnormal anatomy. Across a diverse set of downstream tasks, A4-MR outperforms existing foundation models, including a +1.7 AUROC improvement over MedSigLIP for abnormality detection. Using a frozen encoder, A4-MR also surpasses an end-to-end task-specific MedNeXt model for knee segmentation by +1.4 Dice and performs comparably to the best task-specific model for abdominal organ segmentation on AMOS, within 0.4 Dice. Finally, without anatomical prompts, A4-MR localizes 3D anatomy comparably to MedSAM2 provided with ground-truth bounding boxes. Together, these results demonstrate that anatomy-level multimodal alignment and abnormality-aware representation learning can enable a single MRI foundation model to support localization, segmentation, and pathology-related tasks.
paper.title: A4-MR: Abnormality-aware Anatomical Alignment for MR

paper.abstract: Modern machines can solve equations, follow logic and reason through language, yet they still struggle with problems that require visual non-verbal reasoning. This is evident even in advanced systems such as DeepSeek, ChatGPT and Gemini, which remain limited on visual tasks such as completing abstract patterns or delineating ambiguous regions-of-interest. Unlike explicit intermediate steps in verbal reasoning which can be verified through logic or automated tests, visual reasoning involves implicit intermediate steps with no clear methods for verification. Non-verbal reasoning is therefore challenging to model and, as a result, remains a fundamental limitation of current machine intelligence. Here we introduce GenVerOpt, a general framework that unifies generation, verification and optimisation into a reasoning pipeline for machines. By generating candidate solutions, verifying their correctness, and iteratively refining them, GenVerOpt enables per-sample optimisation rather than relying solely on dataset-level trends captured during model training. This process mirrors human problem-solving where multiple possibilities are imagined, evaluated, and refined until a correct solution emerges. Across diverse domains, GenVerOpt demonstrates capabilities beyond existing systems: it surpasses humans on abstract IQ puzzles, matches clinicians in prostate cancer segmentation, exceeds experts in liver vessel reconstruction and outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in tumour boundary alignment. These results show that machine reasoning can extend beyond language, establishing visual non-verbal reasoning as a foundation for more flexible and generalisable intelligence.
paper.title: Can machines reason non-verbally?

translation.abstract_zh: 现代机器能够解方程、遵循逻辑并通过语言进行推理，但它们在需要视觉非语言推理的问题上仍然举步维艰。这一点即使在DeepSeek、ChatGPT和Gemini等先进系统中也很明显，它们在完成抽象图案或勾画模糊感兴趣区域等视觉任务上仍然受限。与可以通过逻辑或自动化测试验证的语言推理中显式的中间步骤不同，视觉推理涉及隐式的中间步骤，且没有明确的验证方法。因此，非语言推理难以建模，并且因此仍然是当前机器智能的一个根本局限。在此，我们提出GenVerOpt，一个将生成、验证和优化统一为机器推理流程的通用框架。通过生成候选解、验证其正确性并迭代地改进它们，GenVerOpt实现了逐样本优化，而不是仅依赖模型训练期间捕获的数据集层面趋势。这一过程类似于人类解决问题的方式：想象多种可能性，对其进行评估并不断改进，直到出现正确解。在不同领域中，GenVerOpt展现出超越现有系统的能力：在抽象智商谜题上超越人类，在前列腺癌分割上匹配临床医生，在肝血管重建上超越专家，并在肿瘤边界对齐上优于最先进方法。这些结果表明，机器推理可以超越语言，确立视觉非语言推理作为更灵活、更具泛化能力的智能的基础。

paper.abstract: The recent Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3) extends powerful promptable segmentation from spatial cues to concepts, raising the prospect of a single foundation model for universal image segmentation. However, this promise often fails to translate into reliable performance on downstream segmentation tasks. In this work, we empirically identify concept recognition, rather than mask quality, as the primary bottleneck: SAM3 accurately delineates the objects it recognizes yet struggles to robustly determine which concepts are present. Driven by this, we present \textit{\underline{T}ext \underline{A}nchor re-\underline{G}rounding (\TAG{})}, a simple yet effective framework that rectifies the concept recognition of SAM3 on the target domain without dense annotations. Specifically, \TAG{} introduces an \textit{Anchor Residual Pathway} comprising image-conditioned, low-rank adapters to re-ground text anchors in the target distribution and modulate subsequent text-conditioned interactions. Guided solely by image-level category labels, \TAG{} jointly optimizes binary cross-entropy with \textit{Soft Boundary Ranking} objectives to calibrate presence confidence and distinguish present concepts from confusable negatives. Building upon this, we devise \textit{Confidence-Weighted Distillation} to couple rich semantic context of a multimodal large language model with fine-grained spatial priors of SAM3, thereby achieving effective calibration in the absence of manual annotations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that \TAG{} unlocks SAM3's segmentation potential with only 3.1M trainable parameters, achieving impressive performance across diverse scenarios, and notably, even surpassing leading mask-supervised methods on several metrics. \href{https://github.com/MiSsU-HH/TAG_SAM3}{Our code will be publicly available at GitHub \faGithub}.
paper.title: TAG: Calibrating SAM3 for Universal Image Segmentation without Dense Supervision

paper.abstract: Specifying segmentation targets with natural language provides flexible semantic conditioning for medical image segmentation. However, existing methods still struggle to reliably ground high-level textual semantics into accurate pixel-level spatial prompts, especially under low-contrast lesions, ambiguous boundaries, and visually similar anatomical contexts. In this paper, we propose RADAR (Residual Aggregation and Dense Alignment Representations), a parameter-efficient framework for text-guided medical image segmentation. RADAR explicitly decouples and synergizes the medical semantic anchoring capability of BiomedCLIP with the prompt-driven mask decoding ability of MedSAM2, while enabling low-cost task adaptation via LoRA. Specifically, Guided Residual Depth Aggregation adaptively aggregates cross-layer features under semantic guidance to alleviate delayed textual injection and deep semantic dilution. Structured Dense Representation Alignment leverages a frozen BiomedCLIP to construct crop-level target, boundary, and context anchors, improving the local discriminability of dense features and the reliability of automatic prompts. Multi-modal Prompt Generation further converts cross-modal semantic responses into composite text, point, and mask prompts for MedSAM2 decoding. Experiments on three public medical image segmentation datasets show that RADAR achieves competitive performance with only 0.74M trainable parameters, demonstrating its effectiveness in parameter-efficient adaptation, semantic grounding, and dense representation enhancement. The source code is available at https://github.com/JGuiidev/RADAR.

paper.abstract: Depth estimation and Gaussian reconstruction share a need for multi-scale feature processing, yet use different prediction interfaces and training objectives. Whether a decoder's internal computation can be optimized once and reused across these systems remains a structural design question. Search over primitive configurations alone leaves the organization of transformations fixed. To address this gap, we propose GeoBridge, an evolutionary framework for transferable decoder topologies. First, GeoBridge makes stage-internal topology searchable through residual, sequential, and parallel composition of configurable primitives. Shape-preserving composition retains the stage interfaces of a fixed multi-scale scaffold. Second, a functional-tree encoding supports stage-aware crossover and hierarchical mutation, while a gradient sensitivity-alignment proxy evaluates candidates without training. Multi-objective evolution balances this proxy with computation and parameter cost. Third, selected topologies are instantiated and trained in target systems with task-specific prediction interfaces. A single source search takes approximately 12 GPU hours. GeoBridgeNet-A3 achieves the best depth accuracy among four adapted decoder baselines under a common encoder and training protocol on NYU Depth V2 and KITTI. The same topology reaches 27.11 dB PSNR in Gaussian novel-view synthesis on RealEstate10K, and its refined representations support open-vocabulary segmentation on LERF. These results support decoder topology as a reusable design object across the evaluated geometric vision systems. Code and pretrained weights are available at https://github.com/EMI-Group/GeoBridge-NAS.
paper.title: GeoBridge: Evolving Transferable Decoder Topologies for Geometric Vision

paper.abstract: Accurate brain tumor segmentation from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for diagnosis and treatment planning; however, manual delineation is labor-intensive and time-consuming. Existing approaches are either task-specific with limited generalization or rely on user-provided prompts during inference. We present BaT-SAM, a parameter-efficient adaptation framework that enables fully automatic brain tumor segmentation with the Segment Anything Model (SAM). BaT-SAM injects local inductive bias into SAM's frozen Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder via Conv-LoRA, where image features are processed by a sparsely gated mixture of multi-scale convolutional experts. This design compensates for the limited translation-equivariant inductive bias of vanilla ViTs while fine-tuning fewer than 5M parameters (less than 1% of the full model). To remove the need for user prompts, we further introduce a lightweight self-prompting box regressor that is jointly optimized with the adapter using scheduled sampling and predicts tumor locations directly from image embeddings. On the BRISC2025 benchmark, BaT-SAM achieves a weighted mean IoU of 0.832 while outperforming state-of-the-art benchmarks. It further demonstrates strong cross-dataset generalization, achieving Dice scores of 0.702 on Figshare and 0.784 on the LGG MRI Segmentation dataset.
paper.title: BaT-SAM: Introducing Inductive Bias into SAM via a Mixture of Convolutional Experts for Brain Tumor Segmentation
